Compliance Copilot: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Regulatory Document Question Answering

Ankit Kumar Jha
Independent Researcher
India
ankit.aiml625@gmail.com

Abstract - Compliance with regulatory frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, and OWASP security guidelines is a critical challenge for organizations. Legal and engineering teams spend significant effort manually searching large volumes of compliance documentation to answer policy questions. This paper presents Compliance Copilot, a production-ready Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed to automate regulatory question answering with verifiable source citations and built-in safety guardrails. The system employs a multi-stage pipeline: a document ingestion pipeline; a hybrid retrieval strategy combining dense vector search (ChromaDB) and sparse keyword search (BM25) with LLM-driven query expansion; and a generation stage backed by a pluggable LLM factory (supporting Ollama, Groq, HuggingFace, and Mock providers). The system is deployed via Docker and Railway, exposing a FastAPI backend secured by Bearer Token authentication and an interactive Streamlit frontend with built-in analytics. Output quality is structured to be evaluated using the RAGAS framework, while runtime safety is enforced through prompt-injection detection and hallucination grounding checks. This paper contributes a reference architecture for compliance-domain RAG applications, detailing its components, guardrails, and observability stack.

Index Terms - Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Regulatory Compliance, Natural Language Processing, Question Answering, Hybrid Retrieval, BM25, ChromaDB, LangChain, Guardrails

I. INTRODUCTION

The landscape of digital compliance is growing more demanding each year. Enterprises operating under GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and OWASP must maintain up-to-date knowledge of extensive guidelines. A single misinterpretation of a policy can result in regulatory penalties or security breaches. Traditional solutions rely on manual searches through hundreds of pages of documents, which is slow and error-prone. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong natural language understanding, they are prone to hallucination- making up answers when applied outside their training data.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [1] bridges this gap by grounding LLM responses in retrieved, authoritative documents. However, implementing RAG for compliance faces challenges: (1) multi-document synthesis across different frameworks; (2) hallucination risks where LLMs inject unverified technical terms; (3) security vulnerabilities like prompt injection; and (4) the need for exact traceability (document, section, page).

This paper presents Compliance Copilot, an architectural implementation of a RAG system tailored for the compliance domain. Rather than presenting empirical data, this paper details the system’s design, integration of technologies, and built-in mechanisms for safety, observability, and evaluation.

II. RELATED WORK

II. RELATED WORK

Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Lewis et al. [1] introduced RAG as a seq2seq architecture combining a dense retrieval model with a generator. LangChain [2] provides a widely-adopted framework for composing these components. This system builds on LangChain abstractions.

Hybrid Retrieval. Dense vector retrieval captures semantic meaning but may miss exact regulatory terms (e.g., ‘Article 6’). Sparse retrieval via BM25 [3] complements this by matching precise keywords. Ensemble retrieval combining both has been shown to outperform either method alone [4].

Query Expansion and Reranking. Multi-query expansion reformulates the original query to increase recall [5]. Reranking with cross-encoders [6] is a well-established pattern to refine candidate pools retrieved by faster, less precise methods.

LLM Guardrails and Evaluation. Prompt injection attack patterns are a recognized vulnerability [7], while hallucination detection remains an active research area [8]. The RAGAS framework [9] provides metrics for automated evaluation of RAG pipelines.

III. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

The system is designed with scalability, privacy, and security as core tenets. It is organized into distinct layers: User Interface, Backend API, RAG Pipeline, and Data Layer.

(Fig. 1. High-level architecture demonstrating the flow from user query to the FastAPI backend, through the RAG pipeline, and returning a grounded response.)

A. Document Ingestion Pipeline

(Fig. 1. High-level architecture demonstrating the flow from user query to the FastAPI backend, through the RAG pipeline, and returning a grounded response.)

A. Document Ingestion Pipeline

The ingestion pipeline processes various regulatory sources (PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT) into searchable embeddings and keyword indices. Documents are parsed and chunked using a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with a chunk_size=1000 and overlap=200 to preserve regulatory clauses spanning boundaries. Each chunk is enriched with metadata, specifically the compliance category (e.g., GDPR, SOC2, ISO27001, OWASP), source filename, page number, and section. The system utilizes the sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model [10] to convert text into vectors, which are stored locally in ChromaDB [11], alongside a BM25 index for keyword search.

B. Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline

To address the semantic gap while maintaining exact keyword matches, the system implements a hybrid search strategy. A query expansion module first uses the LLM to expand a single user question into three related sub-questions. These queries are executed against both the ChromaDB database and the BM25 index.

 (Fig. 2. Retrieval strategy combining dense semantic (ChromaDB) and sparse keyword (BM25) results with query expansion and reranking.)

The results are merged and reranked using a CrossEncoder from the sentence-transformers library [10] to select the top 5 most relevant paragraphs.

C. Mathematical Formulation of Retrieval

The results are merged and reranked using a CrossEncoder from the sentence-transformers library [10] to select the top 5 most relevant paragraphs.

C. Mathematical Formulation of Retrieval

The final retrieval score used prior to reranking is a weighted ensemble combination of dense semantic similarity and sparse keyword relevance. We define the hybrid score as:

Score_hybrid(d, q) = 0.6 × Score_dense(d, q) + 0.4 × Score_BM25(d, q)

where d is the document chunk and q is the query. This weighting reflects a priority on semantic matching while preserving keyword precision.

The dense score relies on cosine similarity between the query embedding q and document embedding d:

Score_dense(d, q) = (q · d) / (||q|| ||d||)

D. Generation and LLM Factory

The “AI brain” reads the retrieved paragraphs to generate the final answer. The system employs a Factory Pattern supporting four LLM providers: 1. Ollama: Runs open-source models locally, ensuring 100% privacy for sensitive data. 2. Groq: A cloud API providing extremely high-speed inference. 3. HuggingFace: A cloud API for broad access to open-source models. 4. Mock: A simulated LLM that returns dummy answers for automated testing.

IV. SECURITY, GUARDRAILS, AND OBSERVABILITY

A. Safety Guardrails

IV. SECURITY, GUARDRAILS, AND OBSERVABILITY

A. Safety Guardrails

Compliance data requires strict constraints on AI behavior. The system implements a dual-layer guardrail architecture: Input Guardrail: Before AI processing, the user’s question is scanned via regex patterns to block malicious hacking attempts and prompt injections. Output Guardrail: After generating a response, the system checks if the answer uses specific technical terms not found in the retrieved documents. If unverified terms are detected, a hallucination warning is appended.

B. Authentication and Deployment

The backend logic is exposed via a FastAPI Rest application secured by Bearer Token Authentication. Deployment is containerized using Docker and Docker Compose. Cloud deployment is supported via Railway configurations.

C. Frontend Interface

Built using Streamlit, the UI provides interactive chat bubbles, an expandable source citations viewer, an analytics sidebar (displaying total queries and violations), a document upload panel, and policy compliance badges to visually indicate the safety of the response.

D. Observability and Evaluation Framework

LangSmith is integrated to trace operations, logging every step of the pipeline. Furthermore, the architecture is designed to support the RAGAS framework [9] to systematically measure answer quality across four dimensions: Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Context Precision, and Context Recall.

V. DISCUSSION AND LIMITATIONS

A. Architectural Benefits

V. DISCUSSION AND LIMITATIONS

A. Architectural Benefits

The separation of concerns between the Streamlit frontend and the FastAPI backend allows independent scaling. The hybrid retrieval strategy effectively balances the semantic understanding required to interpret vague user queries with the strict keyword matching necessary for legal citations.

B. Limitations and Error Analysis

Several limitations exist: 1. Regex-Based Input Filters: The input guardrail relies on pattern matching, which may be bypassed by novel prompt injection attacks. 2. Output Grounding Constraints: The output guardrail operates on exact keyword verification. Nuanced semantic hallucinations may bypass this filter. 3. Context Window Limits: Extracting only the top 5 paragraphs may not provide sufficient context for highly complex queries requiring synthesis across dozens of regulatory articles.

VI. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK

This paper detailed the architecture of Compliance Copilot, a system designed to address the challenges of regulatory document Q&A through hybrid retrieval, a pluggable LLM factory, and strict safety guardrails. By integrating local embedding capabilities, Docker-based deployment, and a Streamlit analytics dashboard, the system serves as a scalable template for enterprise compliance applications.

Future work will focus on empirical validation. This includes: (1) conducting large-scale quantitative evaluations using the RAGAS framework against a curated benchmark; (2) implementing Natural Language Inference (NLI) models for more robust output hallucination detection; and (3) expanding the ingestion pipeline to support multi-modal compliance documents containing complex tables and architectural diagrams.

REFERENCES

REFERENCES

[1] P. Lewis et al., “Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks,” NeurIPS, vol. 33, pp. 9459-9474, 2020.
[2] H. Chase, “LangChain,” [Online]. Available: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain.
[3] S. E. Robertson and S. Walker, “Some Simple Effective Approximations to the 2-Poisson Model for Probabilistic Weighted Retrieval,” ACM SIGIR, pp. 232-241, 1994.
[4] K. Al-Hazmi and A. Khatri, “Hybrid Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering,” Information Processing & Management, vol. 60, no. 3, 2023.
[5] J. Ma et al., “Zero-Shot Neural Retrieval via Domain-Targeted Synthetic Query Generation,” EMNLP, pp. 1803-1812, 2021.
[6] N. Nogueira and K. Cho, “Passage Re-ranking with BERT,” arXiv:1901.04085, 2019.
[7] F. Perez and I. Ribeiro, “Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models,” arXiv:2211.09527, 2022.
[8] X. Guo et al., “Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Model Generation: A Survey,” ACM Computing Surveys, vol. 56, no. 9, 2024.
[9] S. Es et al., “RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation,” EACL, pp. 150-163, 2024.
[10] N. Reimers and I. Gurevych, “Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks,” EMNLP-IJCNLP, pp. 3982-3992, 2019.
[11] ChromaDB Contributors, “Chroma: The AI-native Open-Source Embedding Database,” GitHub, 2023. [Online]. Available: https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma.
[12] T. Zhang et al., “Semantic Chunking Strategies for Retrieval-Augmented Generation,” arXiv:2401.00368, 2024.

TechNova Employee Handbook 2024
Welcome to TechNova
TechNova Solutions is a software company founded in 2016 in Austin, Texas. We build NovaCloud,
a platform that helps mid-sized companies run and monitor their data pipelines. As of 2024 we
employ 240 people across three offices: Austin, Dublin and Singapore.
This handbook describes how we work together. It applies to all permanent employees. Contractors
are covered by the terms of their individual agreements.
Working Hours
TechNova operates on flexible hours. Employees are expected to be available during the core
hours of 10:00 to 16:00 in their local time zone, and to work an average of 40 hours per week.
Teams hold a daily stand-up inside core hours. Meetings outside core hours should be recorded so
colleagues in other regions can catch up.
Remote Work
All engineering roles are remote-friendly. Employees may work remotely up to four days per week,
and fully remote arrangements are approved case by case by the reporting manager and the
People team.
Employees working remotely from another country for more than 30 days in a calendar year must
notify the People team first, because this can create tax obligations for both the employee and
TechNova.
Annual Leave
Every full-time employee receives 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, in addition to
local public holidays. Leave is accrued monthly at two days per month.
Up to five unused leave days may be carried over into the next year and must be used before 31
March. Leave requests are submitted in the People portal and are normally approved within three

Up to five unused leave days may be carried over into the next year and must be used before 31
March. Leave requests are submitted in the People portal and are normally approved within three
working days.
Sick Leave
Employees receive up to 10 days of paid sick leave per year. A medical certificate is required for
any absence longer than three consecutive working days.
Mental health days count as sick leave. Employees do not have to explain the nature of an illness to
their manager.
Parental Leave
TechNova offers 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to the primary caregiver and 6 weeks to the
secondary caregiver. Leave can be taken in up to three separate blocks during the first 18 months.
Employees returning from parental leave may work a reduced four-day week at 80 percent pay for
the first three months.

Learning Budget
Each employee has an annual learning budget of 1500 USD. It can be spent on courses,
conference tickets, books and certifications. The budget does not carry over to the following year.
Purchases above 500 USD need manager approval in advance. Submit receipts through the
Expenses portal within 30 days of purchase.
Expense Reimbursement
Approved business expenses are reimbursed with the next monthly payroll run, provided the claim
is submitted before the 25th of the month. Claims submitted later are paid the following month.
Travel must be booked through the TechNova travel portal. Economy class is standard for flights
under six hours; business class may be booked for longer flights with director approval.
Equipment Policy
New employees receive a laptop, an external monitor, a keyboard and a mouse. Engineers may
choose between a MacBook Pro and a Dell XPS running Ubuntu. Laptops are refreshed every
three years.
Employees also receive a one-time home office allowance of 600 USD for a desk and chair.
Equipment remains the property of TechNova and must be returned when employment ends.
Performance Reviews
Performance reviews happen twice a year, in March and September. Each review combines a
self-assessment, manager feedback and peer feedback from at least two colleagues.
Promotion decisions and salary adjustments are made during the March cycle. Compensation
changes take effect from 1 May.
Code of Conduct
TechNova does not tolerate harassment, discrimination or bullying of any kind. Concerns can be

changes take effect from 1 May.
Code of Conduct
TechNova does not tolerate harassment, discrimination or bullying of any kind. Concerns can be
raised with a manager, with the People team, or anonymously through the ethics hotline.
All reports are investigated within 10 working days. Retaliation against anyone who raises a
concern in good faith is itself a serious breach of this policy.

NovaCloud Product Guide v4.2
NovaCloud Overview
NovaCloud is TechNova's data pipeline platform. It lets teams build, schedule and monitor pipelines
that move data between databases, object storage and SaaS applications, without managing
servers.
The platform has three parts: the Pipeline Builder, the Scheduler and the Observability Hub. The
current release is NovaCloud 4.2, shipped in February 2024.
Pipeline Builder
The Pipeline Builder is a visual editor where a pipeline is assembled from connectors, transforms
and destinations. Every pipeline can also be exported as a YAML file and stored in Git.
Transforms are written in SQL or Python. Python transforms run in an isolated sandbox with a 10
minute execution limit and 4 GB of memory.
Scheduler
Pipelines can run on a fixed schedule using cron expressions, on an event trigger such as a new
file landing in object storage, or on demand through the REST API.
Failed runs are retried three times with exponential backoff. After the third failure the pipeline is
marked as failed and an alert is sent to the configured notification channel.
Observability Hub
The Observability Hub shows run history, row counts, execution time and data quality checks for
every pipeline. Metrics are retained for 13 months on all paid plans.
Data quality checks include null checks, uniqueness checks, range checks and freshness checks. A
failing check can either warn or stop the pipeline, depending on how it is configured.
Connectors
NovaCloud 4.2 ships with 68 connectors, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery,

failing check can either warn or stop the pipeline, depending on how it is configured.
Connectors
NovaCloud 4.2 ships with 68 connectors, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery,
Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe and Zendesk.
Customers can build private connectors with the Connector SDK. A private connector is visible only
inside the customer's workspace and is not reviewed by TechNova.
Pricing Tiers
NovaCloud has three subscription tiers. Starter costs 99 USD per month and includes 3 pipelines, 1
workspace and 10 GB of monthly data transfer.
Growth costs 499 USD per month and includes 25 pipelines, 3 workspaces and 250 GB of monthly
data transfer. Enterprise is priced per contract and includes unlimited pipelines, unlimited
workspaces, single sign-on and a private deployment option.

Data transfer above the included allowance is billed at 0.09 USD per GB. Usage is measured per
calendar month and shown live in the Billing page.
Platform Limits
A single pipeline may contain up to 150 steps. The maximum size of one file processed in a single
step is 5 GB. The REST API is rate limited to 600 requests per minute per workspace.
Limits can be raised for Enterprise customers by contacting the Technical Account Manager.
Integrations and Alerting
Alerts can be delivered to email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty and any HTTPS webhook.
Each pipeline can have its own alerting rules.
NovaCloud also exposes a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint so customers can pull pipeline
metrics into their own monitoring stack.
Getting Started
After signing up, create a workspace, connect a source, choose a destination and run the pipeline
once manually. The guided tutorial in the console walks through this in about 15 minutes.
Free trials last 14 days and include all Growth tier features. No credit card is required to start a trial.
Deprecation and Versioning
The NovaCloud REST API is versioned. Version v1 is deprecated and will be switched off on 31
December 2024. Version v2 is the current, supported version.
TechNova gives at least 12 months notice before removing an API version, and 6 months notice
before removing a connector.

TechNova Information Security Policy

Purpose and Scope

This Information Security Policy applies to all TechNova employees, contractors and systems that store or process customer data. It is reviewed every 12 months by the Security team and approved by the CTO.

Breaking this policy may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contract.

Password Policy

Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must not be reused across systems. All TechNova employees must store work passwords in the company password manager, 1Password.

Passwords are not rotated on a fixed schedule. Following current NIST guidance, TechNova only forces a password change when there is evidence of compromise. Sharing a password with another person, including a colleague, is never permitted.

Multi-Factor Authentication

Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for every TechNova system that supports it, including email, the production cloud console, the code repository and the VPN.

Hardware security keys or an authenticator app must be used. SMS codes are not accepted as a second factor because of the risk of SIM swapping attacks.

Access Control

Access to production systems follows the principle of least privilege. Engineers receive read-only access by default; write access to production is granted for a maximum of eight hours through the just-in-time access tool.

All access rights are reviewed quarterly. Accounts belonging to people who leave TechNova are disabled within two hours of their final working day.

Data Encryption

All access rights are reviewed quarterly. Accounts belonging to people who leave TechNova are disabled within two hours of their final working day.

Data Encryption

Customer data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher, and at rest with AES-256. Encryption keys are managed in the cloud provider's key management service and rotated annually.

Customer data is never copied to a laptop or a personal device. Debugging is done through approved tooling that masks personally identifiable information.

Device Security

All company laptops have full disk encryption, an automatic screen lock after five minutes, and the company endpoint protection agent installed. Employees must install operating system security updates within 14 days of release.

Lost or stolen devices must be reported to security@technova.example immediately so the device can be remotely wiped.

Incident Response

A security incident is any event that may compromise the confidentiality, integrity or availability of customer data. Anyone who suspects an incident must report it within one hour.

The Security team triages the report, assigns a severity and leads the response. For confirmed breaches of personal data, affected customers and the relevant supervisory authority are notified within 72 hours, as required by GDPR.

Compliance and Certification

TechNova holds a SOC 2 Type II report, renewed annually, and is certified against ISO 27001. Customers can request both reports under a non-disclosure agreement from their account manager.

TechNova holds a SOC 2 Type II report, renewed annually, and is certified against ISO 27001. Customers can request both reports under a non-disclosure agreement from their account manager.

Penetration tests are carried out by an external firm twice a year. A summary of findings is available to Enterprise customers on request.

Vendor Security

Any new vendor that will process customer data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review covers certifications, data location, sub-processors and the vendor's own incident history.

A register of all approved sub-processors is published on the TechNova trust page and updated within 30 days of any change.

Security Training

Every employee completes security awareness training during onboarding and again every 12 months. Engineers additionally complete secure coding training each year.

TechNova runs simulated phishing exercises each quarter. Employees who click a simulated phishing link are enrolled in a short refresher course rather than penalised.

Teams hold a daily stand-up inside core hours. Meetings outside core hours should be recorded so
colleagues in other regions can catch up.
Remote Work

and fully remote arrangements are approved case by case by the reporting manager and the

NovaCloud Product Guide v4.2
NovaCloud Overview
NovaCloud is TechNova's data pipeline platform. It lets teams build, schedule and monitor pipelines
that move data between databases, object storage and SaaS applications, without managing
servers.
The platform has three parts: the Pipeline Builder, the Scheduler and the Observability Hub. The

current release is NovaCloud 4.2, shipped in February 2024.
Pipeline Builder
The Pipeline Builder is a visual editor where a pipeline is assembled from connectors, transforms
and destinations. Every pipeline can also be exported as a YAML file and stored in Git.
Transforms are written in SQL or Python. Python transforms run in an isolated sandbox with a 10

minute execution limit and 4 GB of memory.
Scheduler
Pipelines can run on a fixed schedule using cron expressions, on an event trigger such as a new
file landing in object storage, or on demand through the REST API.
Failed runs are retried three times with exponential backoff. After the third failure the pipeline is
marked as failed and an alert is sent to the configured notification channel.

Observability Hub
The Observability Hub shows run history, row counts, execution time and data quality checks for
every pipeline. Metrics are retained for 13 months on all paid plans.
Data quality checks include null checks, uniqueness checks, range checks and freshness checks. A
failing check can either warn or stop the pipeline, depending on how it is configured.

Pricing Tiers
NovaCloud has three subscription tiers. Starter costs 99 USD per month and includes 3 pipelines, 1
workspace and 10 GB of monthly data transfer.
Growth costs 499 USD per month and includes 25 pipelines, 3 workspaces and 250 GB of monthly

data transfer. Enterprise is priced per contract and includes unlimited pipelines, unlimited
workspaces, single sign-on and a private deployment option.

Data transfer above the included allowance is billed at 0.09 USD per GB. Usage is measured per
calendar month and shown live in the Billing page.
Platform Limits
A single pipeline may contain up to 150 steps. The maximum size of one file processed in a single
step is 5 GB. The REST API is rate limited to 600 requests per minute per workspace.

Limits can be raised for Enterprise customers by contacting the Technical Account Manager.
Integrations and Alerting
Alerts can be delivered to email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty and any HTTPS webhook.
Each pipeline can have its own alerting rules.
NovaCloud also exposes a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint so customers can pull pipeline
metrics into their own monitoring stack.

After signing up, create a workspace, connect a source, choose a destination and run the pipeline
once manually. The guided tutorial in the console walks through this in about 15 minutes.

TechNova Information Security Policy

Purpose and Scope

This Information Security Policy applies to all TechNova employees, contractors and systems that store or process customer data. It is reviewed every 12 months by the Security team and approved by the CTO.

Breaking this policy may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contract.

Password Policy

Password Policy

Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must not be reused across systems. All TechNova employees must store work passwords in the company password manager, 1Password.

Passwords are not rotated on a fixed schedule. Following current NIST guidance, TechNova only forces a password change when there is evidence of compromise. Sharing a password with another person, including a colleague, is never permitted.

Multi-Factor Authentication

Multi-Factor Authentication

Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for every TechNova system that supports it, including email, the production cloud console, the code repository and the VPN.

Hardware security keys or an authenticator app must be used. SMS codes are not accepted as a second factor because of the risk of SIM swapping attacks.

Access Control

Access Control

Access to production systems follows the principle of least privilege. Engineers receive read-only access by default; write access to production is granted for a maximum of eight hours through the just-in-time access tool.

All access rights are reviewed quarterly. Accounts belonging to people who leave TechNova are disabled within two hours of their final working day.
Data Encryption

All access rights are reviewed quarterly. Accounts belonging to people who leave TechNova are disabled within two hours of their final working day.

Data Encryption

Customer data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher, and at rest with AES-256. Encryption keys are managed in the cloud provider's key management service and rotated annually.

Customer data is never copied to a laptop or a personal device. Debugging is done through approved tooling that masks personally identifiable information.

Device Security

Device Security

All company laptops have full disk encryption, an automatic screen lock after five minutes, and the company endpoint protection agent installed. Employees must install operating system security updates within 14 days of release.

Lost or stolen devices must be reported to security@technova.example immediately so the device can be remotely wiped.

Incident Response

Incident Response

A security incident is any event that may compromise the confidentiality, integrity or availability of customer data. Anyone who suspects an incident must report it within one hour.

The Security team triages the report, assigns a severity and leads the response. For confirmed breaches of personal data, affected customers and the relevant supervisory authority are notified within 72 hours, as required by GDPR.

Compliance and Certification

Compliance and Certification

TechNova holds a SOC 2 Type II report, renewed annually, and is certified against ISO 27001. Customers can request both reports under a non-disclosure agreement from their account manager.

Penetration tests are carried out by an external firm twice a year. A summary of findings is available to Enterprise customers on request.

Vendor Security

Vendor Security

Any new vendor that will process customer data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review covers certifications, data location, sub-processors and the vendor's own incident history.

A register of all approved sub-processors is published on the TechNova trust page and updated within 30 days of any change.

Security Training

Security Training

Every employee completes security awareness training during onboarding and again every 12 months. Engineers additionally complete secure coding training each year.

TechNova runs simulated phishing exercises each quarter. Employees who click a simulated phishing link are enrolled in a short refresher course rather than penalised.
